{{Short description|American writer and editor (1960–2026)}}
{{good article}}
[[Image:JRommsm.jpg|upright|thumb|Joe Romm, 2007]]
'''Joseph Jacob Romm''' (June 27, 1960 – September 14, 2026) was an American researcher, author, editor, physicist<ref>Begley, Sharon. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB117096971406102765 "Climate Pessimists Were Right"], ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', February 9, 2007</ref> and climate expert.<ref>Garber, Kent. [https://www.usnews.com/articles/news/energy/2009/03/31/joe-romm-influential-liberal-climate-change-expert-and-blogger.html?loomia_ow=t0:s0:a41:g2:r7:c0.298144:b23521932&s_cid=loomia:epas-lisa-jackson-is-at-the-center-of-obamas-climate-change-policy "Joe Romm, Influential Liberal Climate Change Expert and Blogger"], {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100609005238/http://www.usnews.com/articles/news/energy/2009/03/31/joe-romm-influential-liberal-climate-change-expert-and-blogger.html?loomia_ow=t0%3As0%3Aa41%3Ag2%3Ar7%3Ac0.298144%3Ab23521932&s_cid=loomia%3Aepas-lisa-jackson-is-at-the-center-of-obamas-climate-change-policy |date=2010-06-09 }} ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'', March 31, 2009; and Lloyd Robin. [https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/2009/10/19/geoengineering-wars-another-scientist-teases-out-a-surprising-effect-of-global-deforestation "Geoengineering wars: Another scientist teases out a surprising effect of global deforestation"]. ''Scientific American'', October 19, 2009</ref> He advocated for reducing [[greenhouse gas emissions]] to limit [[global warming]] and increasing [[energy security]] through [[Efficient energy use|energy efficiency]] and [[green energy]] technologies.<ref name=Clean>[http://www.cleanhouston.org/about/romm.htm About Us: Joseph Romm] {{Webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060720182825/http://www.cleanhouston.org/about/romm.htm |date=2006-07-20 }}, Cleanhouston.org, Citizen’s League for Environmental Action Now, Houston, Texas, accessed July 14, 2016</ref> In 2009, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' magazine named Romm to its list of "100 People Who Are Changing America",<ref name=RS>"The 100 People Who Are Changing America", ''Rolling Stone'' magazine, March 18, 2009</ref> and ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine named him one of its "[[Heroes of the Environment (2009)]]", calling him "The Web's most influential climate-change blogger".<ref name=Hero>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090928070059/http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/0,28757,1924149,00.html "Heroes of the Environment 2009"]. ''Time'' magazine, September 2009; and Walsh, Bryan. [https://web.archive.org/web/20090928234734/http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,1924149_1924153_1924209,00.html "Heroes of the Environment 2009 – Activists: Joe Romm"], ''Time'' magazine, September 2009.</ref>

In the 1990s, Romm served as the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary at the [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]] rising to Acting Assistant Secretary. At the [[Center for American Progress]], in 2006, he founded the blog ''Climate Progress'', which became part of the ''[[Think Progress]]'' website. ''Time'' magazine named Romm's blog one of the "Top 15 Green Websites".<ref name=TIME>Roston, Eric. [https://web.archive.org/web/20080421011306/http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1730759_1731034_1731042,00.html "Green Websites: ''Climate Progress''"]. [[Time.com]], April 17, 2008 (originally published in ''Time'' magazine in 2007), accessed November 29, 2010</ref> In 2009, [[Thomas L. Friedman]], in ''[[The New York Times]]'', called ''Climate Progress'' "the indispensable blog",<ref name=TLF/> and ''Time'' included it in a list of the 25 "Best Blogs of 2010".<ref name=BestBlogs>[https://web.archive.org/web/20100629201835/http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/completelist/0,29569,1999770,00.html "Best Blogs of 2010"]. ''Time'' magazine, June 28, 2010</ref> Romm was the chief science advisor for the documentary series ''[[Years of Living Dangerously]]'', which won the 2014 [[Emmy Award]] for Outstanding Documentary or Nonfiction Series.<ref name=YearsEmmy/> In 2019, he founded and served as the first editor-in-chief of the progressive news aggregator ''Front Page Live''. Throughout these decades, he wrote on climate, energy security, as well as language and persuasion, for news sources and journals, and lectured at universities and other organizations. Romm ended his career as a senior research fellow at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]'s Penn Center for Science, Sustainability and the Media, writing white papers about climate disinformation.<ref name=UofPwelcome/>

Romm published ten books and many articles on [[global warming]], clean energy and communications.<ref name=UofPwelcome/> His 2006 book ''[[Hell and High Water (book)|Hell and High Water]]'' summarizes observations and forecasts of [[climate change]], discussed technology and policy solutions, and criticized political disinformation used to undermine climate science.<ref name=Talbot>Talbot, David. [https://www.technologyreview.com/Energy/18301 "Hell and Hydrogen"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414184016/http://www.technologyreview.com/energy/18301/ |date=2012-04-14 }}. ''Technology Review'', March/April 2007 issue, accessed October 29, 2015</ref> His 2015 book, ''Climate Change: What Everyone Needs to Know'', covers basic climate science in a Q&A format.<ref name=Doniger/> He also wrote books on how scientists and activists can communicate more persuasively to explain science and policy to the public. His 2012 book, ''Language Intelligence'', concerns the effective use of rhetoric, and his 2018 book, ''How to Go Viral and Reach Millions'', discusses how to tell scientific stories in ways that draw attention and connect with people emotionally. His 2025 revised edition of ''[[The Hype About Hydrogen]]'' decries what he calls "false promises" made by the fossil fuel industry and sets forth the solutions that Romm says can save the climate.

==Life and career==

===Early life and career===
Romm was born on June 27, 1960, and grew up in [[Middletown, Orange County, New York|Middletown]], New York,<ref name=TimesObit/> the youngest of three sons of Al Romm (1926–1999), managing editor of the ''[[Times Herald-Record]]'' newspaper,<ref>Al Romm was managing editor of the ''[[Times Herald-Record]]'' newspaper from the 1950s into the 1980s. Bedell, Barbara. [http://www.romm.org/obit.html "''Record's'' First Editor Dies"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000421174719/http://romm.org/obit.html |date=2000-04-21 }}, ''Times Herald-Record'', December 1999</ref> and [[Ethel Grodzins Romm]], an author, journalist,<ref name=BWW>[https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/The-Workmens-Circle-to-Honor-Activists-Ethel-Grodzins-Romm-Joe-Romm-at-2016-Winter-Benefit-20161020 "The Workmen's Circle to Honor Activists Ethel Grodzins Romm & Joe Romm at 2016 Winter Benefit"], BroadwayWorld.com, October 20, 2016</ref> project manager,<ref>[[Guy Kawasaki|Kawasaki, Guy]]. ''Hindsights: The Wisdom and Breakthroughs of Remarkable People'', Beyond Words Publishing (1994) {{ISBN|0941831957}}; and Belludi, Nagesh. [https://www.rightattitudes.com/2007/04/01/building-consensus "Ethel Romm on Building Consensus"], RightAttitudes.com, April 1, 2007, accessed July 12, 2016</ref> CEO of an environmental technology company<ref name=NitonAward>Thomson, Elizabeth A. [https://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/1995/lead-1213.html "Lead detector wins R&D award"], MIT News, December 13, 1995, accessed July 12, 2016</ref> and, later, chair of the Lyceum Society of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=BWW/><ref>[http://www.nyas.org/AboutUs/AcademyNews.aspx?cid=aa5fde0c-d77f-4881-b5ea-d807ce03df4f "#IAmNYAS: Ethel Romm"], The New York Academy of Sciences, October 24, 2016</ref> His uncle is physicist [[Lee Grodzins]],<ref>[https://www.recordonline.com/obituaries/n0019562 Obituary: Ethel Grodzins Romm], ''[[Times Herald-Record]]'', December 4, 2021</ref><ref name=NitonAward/> and his aunt was library science expert [[Anne Grodzins Lipow]].<ref>[http://www.sfgate.com/news/article/LIPOW-Anne-Grodzins-2725858.php "Lipow, Anne Grodzins"], Obituary, SFGate.com, September 12, 2004, accessed July 12, 2016; and [http://www.berkeley.edu/news/berkeleyan/2004/10/14_lipow.shtml "Obituary: Anne Lipow"], ''UC Berkeley News'', October 14, 2004, accessed November 22, 2016</ref> Romm graduated from [[Middletown High School (New York)|Middletown High School]] in 1978.<ref>''Epilogue'' yearbook, 1978, [[Middletown High School (New York)|Middletown High School]], p. 95</ref>

[[Image:MIT Main Campus Aerial.jpg|thumb|left|The campus of [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], where Romm earned his Ph.D in physics in 1987.]]
Romm attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1982 and a Ph.D. in 1987, both in [[physics]].<ref name=Arbo>[http://www.aps.org/policy/fellowships/directory.cfm Directory of APS & AIP Congressional Science Fellows: 1987–88] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101126183024/http://aps.org/policy/fellowships/directory.cfm |date=2010-11-26 }} APS.org, accessed November 28, 2010</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Serial No. 110-10 (House Hearing) – Voluntary Carbon Offsets: Getting What You Pay For |url=https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CHRG-110hhrg58085/CHRG-110hhrg58085 |website=GovInfo.gov |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |access-date=2 July 2023 |pages=30–40 |date=18 July 2007}}</ref> In 1987, Romm was awarded an [[American Physical Society]] Congressional Science Fellowship for the [[U.S. House of Representatives]], where he provided science and security policy advice on the staff of Representative [[Charles Edward Bennett|Charles E. Bennett]].<ref name=Arbo/>

From 1988 to 1990, Romm worked as Special Assistant for International Security at the [[Rockefeller Foundation]]. From 1991 to 1993, he was a researcher at the [[Rocky Mountain Institute]].<ref name=EcoSpeakers>[http://ecospeakers.com/speakers/rommj.html "Joe Romm"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160515223240/http://ecospeakers.com/speakers/rommj.html |date=2016-05-15 }}, EcoSpeakers.com, July 8, 2016</ref> He co-authored the 1994 Rocky Mountain Institute Report, ''Greening the Building and the Bottom Line: Increasing Productivity Through Energy-Efficient Design.''<ref>Lehrer, David. [https://cbe.berkeley.edu/centerline/measuring-workplace-productivity-key-variables-and-future-directions "Measuring Workplace Productivity: Key Variables and Future Directions"], Center for the Built Environment, May 15, 2019</ref> For the Global Environment and Technology Foundation, he performed the first environmental analysis of a system integrating cogenerating fuel cells, fly wheels, and [[power electronics]] aimed at achieving very high-availability power.<ref name=CapE>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080621080140/http://www.cap-e.com/mission/default.cfm#joe Profile of Romm], Capital E, accessed November 29, 2010</ref>

In 1992, Romm published ''The Once and Future Superpower'', a book about America's economic, energy and [[environmental security]].<ref>{{cite book| last=Romm |first=Joseph |year=1992|title=The Once and Future Superpower: How to Restore America's Economic, Energy, and Environmental Security| url=https://archive.org/details/oncefuturesuperp00romm| url-access=registration| location=New York|publisher=William Morrow & Co|isbn=9780688118686}} ({{ISBN|0-688-11868-2}})</ref> In 1993, he wrote ''Defining National Security: The Nonmilitary Aspects'', for the [[Council on Foreign Relations]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Romm |first=Joseph | year=1993| title=Defining National Security: The Nonmilitary Aspects|location=Washington|publisher=Council on Foreign Relations}} ({{ISBN|0-87609-135-4}})</ref> His 1994 book, ''Lean and Clean Management'', discusses management techniques that can reduce the impact of manufacturing and other industries on the environment while increasing productivity and profits.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Hardin |first=Judy |title=Review of ''Lean and Clean Management'' |date=Fall 1995 |journal=Whole Earth Review |access-date=November 29, 2010 |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1510/is_/ai_17461907 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709025458/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1510/is_/ai_17461907 |archive-date=July 9, 2012 |via=[[FindArticles]] |url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref>Wernick, Iddo K. "Book Review, ''Lean and Clean Management'', Romm, J.", ''International Journal of Environment and Pollution'' 5(2/3):314-6 1995</ref><ref>Allenby, Braden R. [https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0192512100211001?download=true "Environmental Security: Concept and Implementation"], ''International Political Science Review'', Sage Journals, Volume 21, Issue 1, January 2000</ref> The same year, he co-authored a paper for the [[American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy|ACEEE]] Summer Study on Energy Efficiency in Buildings on "Policies to Reduce Heat Islands".<ref>Budhiraja, Bakul, ''et al''. [https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.4018/IJAGR.2018100103 "Studying Surface and Canopy Layer Urban Heat Island at Micro-Scale Using Multi-Sensor Data in Geographic Information Systems"], ''International Journal of Applied Geospatial Research'', Volume 9, Issue 4, pp. 36–56, October 1, 2018</ref> In 1999, Romm published ''Cool Companies: How the Best Businesses Boost Profits and Productivity by Cutting Greenhouse Gas Emissions''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080621080140/http://www.cap-e.com/mission/default.cfm#joe Profile of Romm], Capital E, accessed November 29, 2010; [http://www.buildings.com/article-details/articleid/1766/title/bio-of-joseph-romm-ph-d.aspx Biography of Romm and list of publications], Buildings.com, February 25, 2004, accessed November 28, 2010</ref><ref>Reviews of ''Cool Companies'' can be found [https://www.sdearthtimes.com/cut_to_chase/ctc_90.html here]. See also Hertsgaard, Mark. [http://www.markhertsgaard.com/articles/115 "Corporate Greenhouse"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071208173042/http://www.markhertsgaard.com/articles/115 |date=2007-12-08 }}. ''The Nation'', July 26, 1999, accessed at markhertsgaard.com, November 28, 2010</ref>

===U.S. Department of Energy===
Romm served as Acting Assistant Secretary of the [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]], in charge of the [[Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy]] in 1997, as Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for the rest of the period from August 1995 through June 1998, and as Special Assistant for Policy and Planning from 1993 to July 1995.<ref>[http://www.buildings.com/article-details/articleid/1766/title/bio-of-joseph-romm-ph-d.aspx "Bio of Joseph Romm, Ph.D"], Buildings.com, February 25, 2004</ref> Romm's projects there included supervising a 1997 comprehensive technical analysis of energy technologies to [[Climate change mitigation|reduce greenhouse gas emissions]] cost-effectively, titled ''Scenarios of U.S. Carbon Reductions''.<ref>[http://enduse.lbl.gov/Projects/5Lab.html Report: "Scenarios of U.S. Carbon Reductions: Potential Impacts of Energy-Efficient and Low-Carbon Technologies by 2010 and Beyond"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080410024349/http://enduse.lbl.gov/projects/5lab.html |date=April 10, 2008}}. Interlaboratory Working Group, The Technology Evaluation Modeling and Assessment Group, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, September 1997 (click on "Acknowledgements"), accessed November 29, 2010</ref>

===1998 to 2006===
Romm was, for several years, the executive director and founder of the [[non-profit]] Center for Energy and Climate Solutions, which developed strategies for saving energy and cutting pollution and [[greenhouse gas emissions]].<ref name=TimesObit/><ref name=EcoSpeakers/> He was also a principal of the Capital E Group, which consulted on [[technology assessment]] and sustainable design services for clean energy technologies.<ref name=Clean/><ref name=CapE/>

[[File:2009-2012 Toyota Prius (ZVW30R) i-Tech liftback (2015-10-18).jpg|thumb|Romm wrote that hybrid cars like the [[Toyota Prius]], [[Battery electric vehicle|BEVs]] and [[Plug-in electric vehicle|PEVs]], are more effective in reducing greenhouse gases than [[hydrogen cars]].]]
During these years, Romm wrote widely on global warming and energy technology solutions. His 2004 book, ''[[The Hype about Hydrogen]]'' (expanded and updated in 2025), argues that delaying the implementation of current green technologies in favor of waiting for technological breakthroughs in [[hydrogen cars]] is a dangerous distraction from reducing greenhouse gas emissions.<ref name=HypeRevised>Romm, Joseph J. [https://islandpress.org/books/hype-about-hydrogen-revised-edition#desc "''The Hype About Hydrogen, Revised Edition''"], ''[[Island Press]]'', accessed April 25, 2025</ref> The book was named one of the best science and technology books of 2004 by [[Library Journal]].<ref>Lautemann, Eva. "''The Hype About Hydrogen'' – Book Review", ''Library Journal'', April 1, 2004, accessed May 3, 2013</ref> In reviewing the book, Daniel I. Sperling, then a member of [[California Air Resources Board]], offered dissenting views.<ref>Ogden, Joan, D. Sperling, and Anthony Eggert, [https://pubs.acs.org/action/showLogin?uri=http%3A%2F%2Fpubs.acs.org%2Fisubscribe%2Fjournals%2Fcen%2F82%2Fi41%2Fhtml%2F8241books.html "Is there hope for hydrogen?"], ''Chemical and Engineering News'', Volume 82, Number 41, pp. 48-49, October 11, 2004.</ref> Also in 2004, Romm wrote the National Commission on Energy Policy's report, "The Car and Fuel of the Future",<ref>[http://www.if.uidaho.edu/~vutgikar/Fall2007/Hydrogen/FutureCar&Fuel.pdf ''The Car and Fuel of the Future''] {{webarchive| url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090205053800/http://www.if.uidaho.edu/~vutgikar/Fall2007/Hydrogen/FutureCar%26Fuel.pdf |date=2009-02-05 }}, 2004, reprinted in ''Energy Policy'', vol. 34, issue 17 (November, 2006) pp. 2609–14, accessed 11 March 2009.</ref> which was rated the #1 Hottest Article on Energy Policy by [[ScienceDirect]].<ref>[http://top25.sciencedirect.com/subject/social-sciences/23/journal/energy-policy/03014215/archive/11/ "Top 25 Hottest Articles"] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120715153934/http://top25.sciencedirect.com/subject/social-sciences/23/journal/energy-policy/03014215/archive/11/ |date=2012-07-15 }}, ScienceDirect.com, January–March 2007, accessed 11 June 2009.</ref> He was also the [[principal investigator]] for the [[National Science Foundation]] project, ''Future Directions for Hydrogen Energy Research and Education'' (2004).<ref name=nsf>[https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward.do?AwardNumber=0400521 Award Abstract], NSF.gov, January 29, 2004</ref> Romm is interviewed in the 2006 documentary film ''[[Who Killed the Electric Car?]]'', in which he argues that the government's "[[hydrogen car]] initiative" was a bad policy choice and a distraction that delayed the exploitation of more promising technologies, such as electric and [[PHEV|hybrid cars]] that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and increase America's [[energy security]].<ref name=EcoSpeakers/><ref>Curry, Andrew. [https://web.archive.org/web/20100516035443/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2010/05/100512-energy-berlin-fuel-cell-rally "Berlin Rallies for a Tricky Oil Alternative"].  ''[[National Geographic News]]'', May 12, 2010</ref>

Romm's 2006 book ''[[Hell and High Water (book)|Hell and High Water]]'' projected a limited window of opportunity to head off the most catastrophic effects of global warming by using emission-cutting technologies.<ref>See [http://www.harpercollins.com/books/9780061172120/Hell_and_High_Water/index.aspx Publisher webpage], and [https://www.thestar.com/Business/article/166819 Review of the book].</ref> [[Tyler Hamilton (reporter)|Tyler Hamilton]], in his review of the book for ''[[The Toronto Star]]'', wrote: "Romm's book presents overwhelming and disturbing evidence that human-caused greenhouse gases are the primary ingredients behind global warming [and] alarming detail on how the U.S. public is being misled by a federal government (backed by conservative political forces) that is intent on inaction, and that's also on a mission to derail international efforts to curb emissions."<ref name=Star>Hamilton, Tyler. [https://www.thestar.com/article/166819 "Fresh alarm over global warming"], ''Toronto Star'', January 1, 2007, accessed 22 October 2009</ref> ''[[Technology Review]]'' wrote that ''Hell and High Water'' "provides an accurate summary of what is known about global warming and climate change, a sensible agenda for technology and policy, and a primer on how political disinformation has undermined climate science."<ref name=Talbot/>

===''Climate Progress'' and later years===
In 2006, Romm became a senior fellow at the [[Center for American Progress]],<ref>[https://www.americanprogress.org/about/staff/romm-joseph/bio "Joseph Romm: Senior Fellow"]. Center for American Progress, accessed August 10, 2016</ref> where he founded their climate blog, ''[[ThinkProgress#Climate Progress|Climate Progress]]'', which focused on climate science, policy and reporting.<ref>Romm, Joseph (ed). [http://thinkprogress.org/romm/issue/ ''Climate Progress'' blog].  ''Climate Progress'', Thinkprogress.org, accessed November 29, 2010</ref> In 2008, ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine named his blog one of the "Top 15 Green Websites", writing that it "counters bad science and inane rhetoric with original analysis delivered sharply. ...  Romm occupies the intersection of climate science, economics and policy. ... On his blog and in his December 2006 book, ''Hell and High Water'', you can find some of the most cogent, memorable, and deployable arguments for immediate and overwhelming action to confront global warming."<ref name=TIME/> In 2010, ''Time'' magazine wrote, "Viewing climate change through the prism of national security, Romm analyzes breaking energy news and the relevant research ... he challenges the beliefs and conclusions of the mainstream media on climate-change issues."<ref name=BestBlogs/> Romm contributed to the site until 2019.<ref name=Doniger>Doniger, David. [https://www.huffingtonpost.com/david-doniger/clean-air-and-climate-cha_b_8906280.html "Clean Air and Climate Change: Two Books to Get You Going"], ''The Huffington Post'', January 2, 2016</ref><ref>Romm, Joe. [https://archive.thinkprogress.org/scientists-hold-funeral-for-first-icelandic-glacier-killed-by-global-warming-5df0d504809b "'Only you know if we did it': Scientists write dire letter to the future about climate change"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820030350/https://archive.thinkprogress.org/scientists-hold-funeral-for-first-icelandic-glacier-killed-by-global-warming-5df0d504809b/ |date=2020-08-20 }}, ThinkProgress, August 18, 2019</ref> He also wrote for other energy and news sites, including ''[[The Huffington Post]]'',<ref>Romm, Joseph.  [https://www.huffingtonpost.com/joseph-romm/can-obama-stop-the-nuclea_b_163110.html "Can Obama Stop the Nuclear Bomb in the Senate Stimulus Plan?"] ''The Huffington Post'', February 2, 2009; [https://www.huffingtonpost.com/joseph-romm/bill-gates-is-wrong-about_b_462654.html "Bill Gates Is Wrong About 'Energy Miracles'"], ''The Huffington Post'', 15 February 2010</ref> ''[[Grist Magazine|Grist]]'',<ref>Romm, Joseph. [https://www.grist.org/article/2009-03-16-five-steps-to-greener-home "First five steps to a greener home...."] ''Grist'', March 16, 2009; [https://www.grist.org/article/congress-reverses-chus-decision-flushes-100-million-down-the-toilet-pursuin "Stop the madness!: Congress reverses Chu's decision, flushes $100 million down the toilet pursuing hydrogen cars"], ''Grist'', July 23, 2009; and [https://www.grist.org/article/2011-02-11-saudi-arabian-reserves-overstated-by-40-global-production "Saudi Arabian reserves overstated by 40 percent, global production plateau imminent"], ''Grist'', February 11, 2011</ref> ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]'',<ref>Romm, Joseph. [https://www.slate.com/id/2176639 October 2007 article by Romm in ''Slate'']</ref> [[CNN]],<ref>Romm, Joseph [https://www.cnn.com/2022/09/16/opinions/king-charles-environment-climate-change-commonwealth-romm "Opinion: The one political issue Charles should keep speaking out on"], CNN, September 16, 2022</ref> [[Salon.com]]<ref>[https://www.salon.com/news/opinion/feature/2010/05/17/warming_continues_open2010 "We're breaking all kinds of temperature records"], May 17, 2010; [https://www.salon.com/news/environment/feature/2009/01/26/obama_cabinet "Real science comes to Washington"], January 26, 2009; [http://www.salon.com/news/feature/2008/06/30/climate_act/index.html "Anti-science conservatives must be stopped"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216024037/http://www.salon.com/news/feature/2008/06/30/climate_act/index.html |date=2008-12-16 }}, June 30, 2008; [https://www.salon.com/news/feature/2008/04/14/solar_electric_thermal "The technology that will save humanity"], April 14, 2008; and [https://www.salon.com/news/feature/2008/01/22/plug_in_hybrids "The car of the future is here"], January 22, 2008.</ref> and ''[[The New York Times]]''.<ref name=dustbowl>Romm, Joseph. [https://www.nytimes.com/roomfordebate/2012/07/25/how-can-we-prevent-another-dust-bowl/without-carbon-controls-we-face-a-dust-bowl "Without Carbon Controls, We Face a Dust Bowl"], ''The New York Times'', 25 July 2012</ref>

Romm testified before congressional committees about how government action can curb global warming.<ref>See, for example, his [http://enduse.lbl.gov/projects/rommtestimony000921.pdf September 2000 testimony before the Senate Committee on Commerce] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080625062600/http://enduse.lbl.gov/projects/rommtestimony000921.pdf |date=2008-06-25 }}; his [http://www.brdisolutions.com/Site%20Docs/romm.pdf March 2004 testimony before the House Science Committee] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080625062600/http://www.brdisolutions.com/Site%20Docs/romm.pdf |date=2008-06-25}}; his [https://www.markey.senate.gov/GlobalWarming/tools/assets/files/0025.pdf July 2007 testimony before the House Select Committee on Energy Independence & Global Warming]; his [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dVhOyuO6LFM 2012 testimony before the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests and Public Lands] and the [https://www.congress.gov/congressional-report/112th-congress/house-report/519 House Energy & Commerce Committee]; and his [https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CHRG-111hhrg63079/pdf/CHRG-111hhrg63079.pdf 2010 testimony before the House Ways and Means Committee].</ref> In 2007, he testified before the House [[United States House Committee on Science and Technology|Committee on Science and Technology]] on the subject of "Fuels for the Future", specifically the use of liquid fuel from coal and its potential to accelerate global warming.<ref>[https://www.americanprogress.org/issues/green/report/2007/09/05/3525/fuels-for-the-future-romms-testimony-to-congress "Fuels for the Future: Romm’s Testimony to Congress"] AmericanProgress.org, September 5, 2007, accessed August 25, 2016</ref> He lectured on energy technology, global warming and how the media portrays climate change.<ref>See, e.g., [http://www.honorscollege.pitt.edu/climate-change-series "UHC Climate Change Series"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307103532/http://www.honorscollege.pitt.edu/climate-change-series |date=2014-03-07 }}, [[University of Pittsburgh]], April 2013; [https://web.archive.org/web/20070208084139/http://webcast.berkeley.edu/events/details.php?webcastid=15730 "Energy Symposium: The Rosenfeld Effect"]. UCAL Berkeley, 2006; [http://www.yale.edu/opa/newsr/06-09-18-05.all.html "Climate Expert to Discuss Global Warming Solutions"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070224015331/http://www.yale.edu/opa/newsr/06-09-18-05.all.html |date=2007-02-24 }}. Yale University, 2006; and [https://www.hks.harvard.edu/sts/events/workshops/unrulydemocracy.html "Unruly Democracy: Science Blogs and the Public Sphere"]. Harvard, April 2010.</ref>

''[[TreeHugger]]'' describes Romm's 2010 book, ''[[Straight Up (book)|Straight Up]]'', as "a whirlwind tour through the state of climate change, the media that so badly neglects it, the politicians who attempt to address it (and those who obstruct their efforts and ignore [the] science), and the clean energy solutions that could help get us out of the mess".<ref name=Merchant>Merchant, Brian. [http://www.treehugger.com/files/2010/04/straight-up-tackles-climate-blog-era-book-review.php "''Straight Up'' Tackles Climate in the Blog Era"]. ''Treehugger.com'', April 22, 2010</ref><ref>Hamilton, Tyler. "Wente continues to mislead, misinform Canadian public", ''TheEnergyCollective.com'', April 11, 2010</ref> His 2012 book, ''Language Intelligence'', concerns persuasion and the effective use of rhetoric, presenting "Solutions the reader can use for speeches, social media, or just winning the debate around the kitchen table."<ref>[[Ed Markey|Markey, Ed]]. [https://www.huffingtonpost.com/rep-ed-markey/friends-with-words-a-revi_b_1774183.html "Friends With Words: A Review of Joe Romm's New Book ''Language Intelligence''], ''Huffington Post'', August 13, 2012</ref><ref>[[Chris Mooney (journalist)|Mooney, Chris]]. [https://www.pointofinquiry.org/joe_romm_language_intelligence "Joe Romm – Language Intelligence"], ''[[Point of Inquiry]]'', August 13, 2012</ref> Romm's August 2012 article for ''Time'' used the research from ''Language Intelligence'' to analyze whether [[Mitt Romney]] or [[Barack Obama]] was the more effective communicator.<ref name=Time2012>Romm, Joseph. [https://ideas.time.com/2012/08/14/who-is-a-better-communicator-romney-or-obama/ "Who Is the Better Communicator: Romney or Obama?"] ''Time'' magazine, August 14, 2012</ref> Romm encouraged scientists to use the principles of effective communication outlined in the book (instead of their accustomed, technical, neutral style) to better explain the dangers of, and solutions to, climate change to non-scientists and the media.<ref>Cowan, Emery. [http://azdailysun.com/news/local/why-climate-change-communication-isn-t-working/article_4a83cb9e-cdc1-5b44-9029-1f84919c5a99.html "Why climate change communication isn't working"], ''[[Arizona Daily Sun]]'', April 24, 2015</ref>

Romm was the chief science editor for the documentary TV series ''[[Years of Living Dangerously]]'', about the impact of and solutions to climate change. The first season of the series in 2014 on the [[Showtime (TV channel)|Showtime]] network<ref>[http://yearsoflivingdangerously.com/science-advisor/joseph-romm-ph-d/ "Joseph Romm, Ph.D., Chief Science Advisor"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140418220557/http://yearsoflivingdangerously.com/science-advisor/joseph-romm-ph-d/ |date=2014-04-18 }}, ''Years of Living Dangerously'', Showtime, accessed April 18, 2014; Howland, Kara. [https://www.tvgoodness.com/2014/04/13/years-of-living-dangerously-premiere-preview-dry-season-video-interview/ "Years of Living Dangerously Premiere Preview ... FAQ by Joe Romm, Ph.D."], ''TV Goodness'', April 13, 2014; and [https://www.democracynow.org/2014/4/11/years_of_living_dangerously_james_cameron "''Years of Living Dangerously'': James Cameron, Matt Damon, Harrison Ford in TV Climate Change Series"], ''Democracy Now!'', April 11, 2014: Interview with Romm begins at 32:35, and full transcript is linked.</ref> won the 2014 [[Emmy Award]] for Outstanding Documentary or Nonfiction Series.<ref name=YearsEmmy>[https://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2014/08/16/creative-arts-emmys-doled-out-in-hollywood/ "Creative Arts Emmys Doled Out in Hollywood"], CBS Local, August 16, 2014</ref> Romm wrote "Climate Change 101: An Introduction", for the series's website.<ref>Romm, Joseph. [https://web.archive.org/web/20140409231925/http://yearsoflivingdangerously.com/blog/climate-change-101-introduction/ "Climate Change 101: An Introduction"], ''Years of Living Dangerously'', Showtime, accessed April 18, 2014</ref> A second season ran in 2016 on the [[National Geographic Channel]].<ref>[http://www.wri.org/events/2016/10/years-living-dangerously "Years of Living Dangerously"], [[World Resources Institute]], accessed November 21, 2016</ref> In 2015, [[The Weather Channel]] included Romm as one of "the world's 25 most compelling voices" on climate.<ref>[http://weather.climate25.com/ Home page for ''The Climate 25''], The Weather Channel, accessed June 15, 2015</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150625022019/http://weather.climate25.com/project/joe-romm/ "Joe Romm: We can save the world from hundreds of years of misery"], The Weather Channel, accessed June 15, 2015</ref> That year, Romm also wrote the book ''Climate Change: What Everyone Needs to Know'', a primer on the topic.<ref name=Doniger/><ref>[[John Abraham (professor)|Abraham, John]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2015/nov/17/book-review-climate-change-what-everyone-needs-to-know?CMP=share_btn_fb "Book review: Climate Change, What Everyone Needs to Know"], ''The Guardian'', November 17, 2015; and Whitney, Jake. [https://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2016/01/11/the-climate-change-book-the-gop-needs-to-read.html "The Climate Change Book the GOP Needs to Read"], ''The Daily Beast'', January 11, 2016</ref> Ralph Benko in ''[[Forbes]]'' magazine wrote that the "book ... lucidly presents the case both for deep concern and optimism".<ref>Benko, Ralph. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/ralphbenko/2016/04/22/happy-earth-day-how-to-use-capitalism-to-bring-us-abundant-cheap-and-emission-free-energy/#77f37c0d7f71 "Happy Earth Day: How to Use Capitalism to Bring Us Abundant, Cheap and Emission-Free Energy"], ''Forbes'' magazine, April 22, 2016</ref> In ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' magazine, David Wallace-Wells cited the book as an "authoritative primer",<ref>Wallace-Wells, David. [https://nymag.com/daily/intelligencer/2017/07/climate-change-earth-too-hot-for-humans.html "The Uninhabitable Earth"], ''New York'' magazine, July 9, 2017</ref> and in 2026, [[Clay Risen]], in ''The New York Times'', referred to it as "the standard primer for would-be climate-policy debaters".<ref name=TimesObit>Risen, Clay. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/06/climate/joe-romm-dead.html "An Influential Voice in the Climate Debate Has Died at 66"], ''The New York Times'', October 6, 2026</ref> Romm's 2018 book, ''How to Go Viral and Reach Millions'', "teaches everything from word choice to how to recast your scientific stories in ways that connect with people emotionally".<ref>Abraham, John. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2018/jun/27/trump-should-inspire-us-all-but-not-in-the-way-you-might-guess "Trump should inspire us all, but not in the way you might guess"], ''The Guardian'', June 27, 2018</ref>

In June 2019, Romm founded a progressive news aggregator, ''Front Page Live'', together with [[Carl Cameron]], [[Laura Dawn]], [[Sunny Hundal]], [[Helen Stickler]] and others.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wise |first1=Justin |title=Former Fox News reporter says he left because of 'partisan misinformation' |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/media/450079-former-fox-news-reporter-says-he-left-because-of-partisan-misinformation |access-date=14 May 2026 |work=The Hill |date=24 June 2019}}</ref> Romm was its first editor-in-chief.<ref name=TimesObit/><ref>[[Erik Wemple|Wemple, Erik]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2019/06/24/ex-fox-newser-carl-cameron-takes-his-unfinished-business-progressive-startup "Ex-Fox Newser Carl Cameron takes his 'unfinished business' to progressive startup"], ''The Washington Post'', June 24, 2019</ref> In 2023, he became a senior research fellow at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]'s Penn Center for Science, Sustainability and the Media.<ref name=UofPwelcome>{{cite news |title=PCSSM Welcomes Senior Research Fellow Dr. Joseph Romm |work=[[University of Pennsylvania]] |date=June 27, 2023 |url=https://web.sas.upenn.edu/pcssm/news/pcssm-welcomes-senior-research-fellow-dr-joseph-romm/}}</ref> He received a 2024 [[Ban Ki-moon]] Award for Environmental Leadership.<ref>[https://www.asiainitiatives.org/event-gala-2024 "Gala 2024"], ''Asia Initiatives'', September 25, 2024</ref> Romm hosted a weekly podcast from 2025 to 2026, together with his daughter, called ''Decoding [[Taylor Swift]]: A Storytelling Revolution'', analyzing Swift's storytelling techniques and the use of poetic rhetoric in her lyrics to communicate and persuade.<ref name=TimesObit/><ref>[https://yaleclimateconnections.org/2025/09/what-taylor-swift-can-teach-us-about-talking-about-climate-change "What Taylor Swift can teach us about talking about climate change"], ''Yale Climate Connections'', September 15, 2025</ref> It ranked as high as number two in the music category on Apple Podcasts.<ref>{{cite news |last=Moser |first=Erica |title=Taylor Swift, storytelling, and climate communication |work=Penn Today |date=October 10, 2025 |url=https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/taylor-swift-storytelling-and-climate-communication-joe-romm}}</ref> The same year, he was lead author on the study "Are Carbon Offsets Fixable?"<ref>Toussaint, Kristin. [https://www.fastcompany.com/91417775/its-official-25-years-of-evidence-proves-carbon-offsets-dont-work "It’s official: 25 years of evidence proves carbon offsets don’t work"], ''Fast Company'', October 8, 2025</ref> The study found that 90% of [[Carbon offsets and credits|carbon credits]] fail to achieve real-world carbon reduction, and the credits' "intractable problems have persisted despite more than two decades of efforts at market reform and seem unlikely to be resolved"; it suggests that because they create a false sense of progress, they serve to delay policy action to reduce emissions.<ref>Zinin, Andrew. [https://phys.org/news/2025-10-carbon-offsets-years-phased.html  "Carbon offsets have failed for 25 years, and most should be phased out"], [[University of Oxford]] via [[Phys.org]], October 14, 2025</ref><ref>[https://www.smithschool.ox.ac.uk/news/carbon-offsets-have-failed-25-years-and-most-should-be-phased-out-research-0 "Carbon offsets have failed for 25 years, and most should be phased out"], Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment, October 6, 2025</ref>

===Personal life and death===
After 1993, Romm lived in Washington, D.C. From 1994 through 2007, he was a regular contributor to [[The Style Invitational]], a weekly humor contest run by ''The Washington Post''. Among his submissions was the winning entry of what was later declared to be the best overall week's results of the Style Invitational's first decade.<ref>''The Washington Post'', March 9, 2003, p. F5</ref> He was divorced and had one daughter.<ref name=":1" /> 

Romm died by suicide in Washington, on September 14, 2026, at the age of 66.<ref name=TimesObit/><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Remembering Dr. Joe Romm – Penn Center for Science, Sustainability, and the Media |url=https://web.sas.upenn.edu/pcssm/news/remembering-dr-joe-romm/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |language=en-US}}</ref>

[http://dotearth.blogs.nytimes.com/2008/11/03/a-final-campaign-focus-coal-and-co2/?scp=1&sq=Joe%20Romm&st=cse "A final campaign focus: Coal and CO<sub>2</sub>"], ''The New York Times'', November 3, 2008</ref> and the futility of hydrogen for transportation<ref>Wald, Matthew. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/23/opinion/climate-change-carbon-offsets.html "To Fight Climate Change, We Need a Better Carbon Market"], ''The New York Times'', August 23, 2023</ref><ref>Coy, Peter. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/12/08/opinion/carbon-capture-climate-change.html "Carbon Capture Won't Save Us from Climate Change"], ''The New York Times'', December 8, 2023</ref> In 2025 Michael Barnard wrote in CleanTechnica: "Romm ... one of the clearest-eyed analysts of carbon policy and energy technologies ... dismantles the case for [[BECCS]] with forensic clarity. ... He shows how BECCS not only diverts policy and funding away from real decarbonization, but also opens up dangerous land-use pressures that displace food, ecosystems, and people."<ref>Barnard, Michael [https://cleantechnica.com/2025/04/13/yara-orsted-and-the-e200-ton-mirage-what-northern-lights-really-teaches-us-about-ccs "Yara, Ørsted, and the €200/ton Mirage: What Northern Lights Really Teaches Us About CCS"], CleanTechnica, April 13, 2025</ref> The same year, Romm was quoted in ''[[Chemical & Engineering News]]'' discussing [[green hydrogen]].<ref>Bettenhausen, Craig. [https://cen.acs.org/energy/hydrogen-power/Green-hydrogen-still-making-gains/103/web/2025/05 "Green hydrogen is still making gains"], ''[[Chemical and Engineering News]]'', May 8, 2025</ref> 

==Political views==
[[File:Alternative Energies.jpg|right|thumb|300px|Romm argued that rapid deployment of current carbon-reducing technologies is essential to [[global warming mitigation|mitigate the worst effects of global warming]] and preserve both the world economy and a comfortable climate.]]
''[[The New York Times]]'' "Dot Earth" column reviewed Romm's views on global warming solutions in 2008, including his belief that, to combat global warming, humans cannot wait for new technologies and scientific breakthroughs; that instead we must "deploy existing and near-term low-carbon technologies as fast as is humanly possible".<ref name=Dot2008>Revkin, Andrew C. [http://dotearth.blogs.nytimes.com/2008/11/24/joe-romm-on-hansens-mistakes-caps-limits "Joe Romm on Hansen’s Mistakes, Cap’s Limits"], Dot Earth, ''The New York Times'', November 24, 2008</ref> ''The New York Times'' also quoted Romm as stating that, to solve the climate crisis, "We will need a WWII-style approach."  The article noted Romm's belief that "credible people" and the press should publicly support the notion that government action is needed to help solve the global warming crisis.  In particular, the press should explain how current news stories, such as hurricanes, droughts and insect infestations are related to global warming.<ref name=Dot2008/>

According to ''U.S. News & World Report'', Romm believed that global warming "is advancing more swiftly than most people think and than the mainstream media usually report. He has called for significantly ramping up government spending on clean energy technology, halting the construction of new coal plants, rapidly increasing the use of energy-efficient technologies, and imposing a [[emissions trading|cap and trade]] system to sharply limit carbon dioxide emissions."<ref name=Driving/> In 2006, in a radio interview, Romm stated, "Global warming is going to transform this country and our transportation and the way we live our lives.  If we don't act pretty soon, in an intelligent fashion, then change will be forced upon us by the radically changed climate ...  global warming is the issue of the century."<ref>[http://www.calcars.org/calcars-news/333.html "Earth & Sky interviews Joseph Romm about future cars"], Earth & Sky transcript from Calcars.org, March 21, 2006, accessed 23 October 2009.</ref>

In 2011, Romm wrote that "Feeding some 9 billion people by mid-century in the face of a rapidly worsening climate may well be the greatest challenge the human race has ever faced."<ref name=Desertification>Romm, Joseph. [https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v478/n7370/full/478450a.html ''The next dust bowl''], ''Nature'', vol. 478, pp. 450–451, 27 October 2011</ref> Romm's 2010 book, ''Straight Up'' argues: "the bottom line is that the economic cost of action is low, whereas the cost of inaction is incalculably greater." Romm calculated that deployment of existing technologies on the massive scale that can save the climate can be accomplished at the cost of 0.12 percent of global GDP per year. He also asks in the book, "will the United States be a global leader in creating jobs and exports in clean energy technologies, or will we be importing them from Europe, Japan, and the likely clean energy leader in our absence, China."<ref>Kreindler, Tony. [https://blogs.edf.org/climate411/2010/04/19/joe-romm%E2%80%99s-straight-up-is-a-great-resource-for-fact-seekers-on-climate/ "Joe Romm's ''Straight Up'' is a great resource for fact seekers on climate"], [[Environmental Defense Fund]], April 19, 2010</ref> In 2005, with respect to the U.S. Congress's actions on climate, including its votes on the [[XL Pipeline]], Romm told ''The Guardian'': "Future generations suffering from the consequences of our inaction will be bewildered that the legislative body of the richest country in the world could devote so little effort to ameliorating the climate problem and so much effort to making it worse."<ref>Abraham, John. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2015/feb/25/with-climate-change-us-presidents-matter "With climate change, US presidents matter"], ''The Guardian'', February 25, 2015</ref> He believed that [[carbon capture and storage]] and other carbon removal efforts are not scalable solutions, and {{Double+single}}net zero' is just a dangerous myth" used to excuse inaction on the climate crisis.<ref name=Magubane>{{cite news |last=Magubane |first=Nathi |title=Carbon capture and common misconceptions: A Q&A with Joe Romm |work=Penn Today |date=November 8, 2023 |url=https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/carbon-capture-and-common-misconceptions-qa-joe-romm}}</ref><ref>Romm, Joseph. [https://web.archive.org/web/20231220134344/https://themessenger.com/opinion/climate-change-energy-orwellian-outcome-cop28-breakthrough-deal-fossil-fuels "An Orwellian Outcome for COP28’s ‘Breakthrough’ Climate Deal"], ''[[The Messenger (website)|The Messenger]]'', December 20, 2023</ref> In 2025, Romm wrote that [[small modular reactor]]s are a "pipe dream" and the most expensive form of electricity generation, while wind, solar and batteries have become the cheapest.<ref>[https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2025-04-18/small-modular-reactors-cost-california "Small nuclear reactors are no fix for California’s energy needs"], ''Los Angeles Times'', April 18, 2025</ref>

Romm was critical of media coverage of global warming. In his 2010 book, ''[[Straight Up (book)|Straight Up]]'', he wrote that newspapers have most often repeated the views "of U.S. scientists ... receiving funds from the fossil fuel industry [instead] of the world's leading climate scientists. No surprise that much of the public has ended up with a misimpression about the remarkable strength of our scientific understanding and the need for action" and "more and more pieces are being written by senior political reporters, who know very little about global warming."<ref>Romm (2010), Chapter 1</ref> Romm also believed that scientists and politicians need to be more effective communicators about climate change.<ref>Mooney, Chris. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/blog/2012/oct/10/joe-romm-climate-change-political-strategy "Joe Romm on why climate change is a winning political strategy"], ''[[The Guardian]]'', October 10, 2012</ref>

==Reception==
[[Clay Risen]] wrote in ''The New York Times'': "Politicians in government and experts in the field quickly took notice of Mr. Romm's clear, detailed policy takes – and takedowns. ... [M]any credited [Romm with] shaping climate policy during the presidencies of Barack Obama and Joseph R. Biden Jr." Risen also called Romm a "compelling speaker".<ref name=TimesObit/> In 2008, Romm was elected a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] for "distinguished service toward a sustainable energy future and for persuasive discourse on why citizens, corporations, and governments should adopt sustainable technologies".<ref>[http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/full/322/5909/1806 "AAAS Members Elected as Fellows"], ''[[Science (magazine)|Science]]'', December 19, 2008, Vol. 322, no. 5909, pp. 1806-10</ref><ref>[http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2008/1218fellows.shtml "News Archives: AAAS Members Elected as Fellows"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100314011624/http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2008/1218fellows.shtml |date=2010-03-14 }}, aaas.org, 19 December 2008, accessed 21 February 2010.</ref> In 2009, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' magazine named Romm to its list of "100 People Who Are Changing America", quoting journalist David Roberts as follows: "Joe combines two qualities you don't often find together. A deep knowledge of technology, policy and science along with genuine moral passion."<ref name=RS/> Former [[Houston, Texas]], mayor [[Bill White (Texas politician)|Bill White]] called Romm "the nation’s leading expert on energy efficiency".<ref>McDonald, Erika. [http://www.cleanhouston.org/engromm2.asp "An Evening with Joe Romm, Author of ''The Hype About Hydrogen''"]{{Dead link|date=February 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, Citizen's League for Environmental Action Now, 2004, accessed 23 January 2010.</ref> ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'' featured Romm as one of eight "key players" who were "Driving Public Policy in Washington", calling Romm an "oft-cited expert on climate change issues, and a go-to witness at congressional hearings".<ref name=Driving>Garber, Kent. "Driving Public Policy in Washington", ''U.S. News & World Report'', p. 39, vol. 146, no. 3, April 2009 (online at [https://www.usnews.com/articles/news/energy/2009/03/31/joe-romm-influential-liberal-climate-change-expert-and-blogger.html?loomia_ow=t0:s0:a41:g2:r7:c0.298144:b23521932&s_cid=loomia:epas-lisa-jackson-is-at-the-center-of-obamas-climate-change-policy "Top Energy Player: Joe Romm, Influential Liberal Climate Change Expert and Blogger"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100609005238/http://www.usnews.com/articles/news/energy/2009/03/31/joe-romm-influential-liberal-climate-change-expert-and-blogger.html?loomia_ow=t0%3As0%3Aa41%3Ag2%3Ar7%3Ac0.298144%3Ab23521932&s_cid=loomia%3Aepas-lisa-jackson-is-at-the-center-of-obamas-climate-change-policy |date=2010-06-09 }})</ref> ''Time'' magazine named Romm one of its "[[Heroes of the Environment (2009)]]", writing, "He combines ... intellect with a strong sense of moral outrage.  He also possesses a [[Jon Stewart]]-like quality for pointing out the absurdity of his opponents."<ref name=Hero/> ''Time'' named his blog as one of the "Top 15 Green Websites" in 2009.<ref name=TIME/> The same year, [[Thomas L. Friedman]], in ''The New York Times'', called ''Climate Progress'' "the indispensable blog".<ref name=TLF>Friedman, Thomas L. [https://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/08/opinion/08friedman.html?_r=2 "The Inflection Is Near?"], ''The New York Times'', March 7, 2009</ref>

In 2010, ''Time'' included Romm's blog in a list of the 25 "Best Blogs of 2010"<ref name=BestBlogs/> and one of the "Top Five Blogs ''TIME'' Writers Read Daily".<ref>Walsh, Bryan. [https://web.archive.org/web/20100630090632/http://www.time.com/time/video/player/0,32068,104488320001_2000153,00.html "Top Five Blogs ''Time'' Writers Read Daily"], ''Time Video'', 2010, accessed April 10, 2012</ref> The same year, [[TreeHugger]] named Romm's blog the "Best Politics Website", adding, "this is the art of blogging at its best."<ref>McDermott, Matthew. [http://www.treehugger.com/galleries/2010/04/best-of-green-2010-business-politics.php?page=6 "Best Politics Website: ''Climate Progress''"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412132834/http://www.treehugger.com/galleries/2010/04/best-of-green-2010-business-politics.php?page=6 |date=2010-04-12 }}. TreeHugger.com, April 8, 2010</ref> The UK's ''[[The Guardian]]'' ranked ''Climate Progress'' at the top of its list of blogs in its "Top 50 Twitter climate accounts to follow".<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/environment/blog/2010/may/11/top-50-twitter-climate-accounts "Top 50 Twitter climate accounts to follow"].  ''The Guardian'': Environment Blog, May 11, 2010</ref> Reviewing Romm's 2010 book ''Straight Up'', [[Bill McKibben]] wrote that Romm "has been a persuasive voice [warning that] global warming ... is a far worse problem than either politicians or the general public understand [but] that we have much of the technology necessary to at least begin tackling the problem". He called Romm "a tireless foil to the 'right-wing disinformation machine' that has [delayed] action by confusing and disheartening Americans about global warming. ...  It requires a thick skin to take on the daily task of dealing with the disinformers [and] talent as well."<ref>McKibben, Bill, [http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Climate+of+opinion%3A+blogger+Joe+Romm+drives+the+global+warming+debate...-a0231408228 "Climate of Opinion"], ''Washington Monthly'', reproduced in TheFreeLibrary.com, July/August 2010</ref> In 2011, ''The New York Times'' called Romm "one of the country’s most influential writers on climate change".<ref>Broder, John M. [https://www.nytimes.com/2011/03/11/science/earth/11climate.html?hpw "House Panel Votes to Strip E.P.A. of Power to Regulate Greenhouse Gases"]. ''The New York Times'', March 10, 2011</ref> In 2012, ''Planetsave'' wrote that Romm is "considered the world's best blogger on climate science, and politics related to it".<ref>Shahan, Zachary. [https://planetsave.com/2012/02/22/joe-romm-slams-nytimes-climate-journalist-andrew-revkin-contextualizes-heartland-gleick-volcano/ "Joe Romm Slams ''NYTimes'' Climate Journalist Andrew Revkin (& Contextualizes Heartland-Gleick Volcano)"], ''Planetsave'', February 22, 2012</ref> Michael Mann said of Romm, "There’s nobody else who brought all of these interlocking talents and proclivities together in the way that he did. That gave him such a unique voice, and it’s a voice that we sorely could use today."<ref name=TimesObit/>
